requirement_groups.name: Computer Science
requirement_groups.source_instruction: Three Computer Science courses are required. To maintain normal progress toward the Information Systems degree, students must complete 15-121 Introduction to Data Structures prior to the start of Spring Semester, second-year. Students entering the program as freshmen will have the option to complete a Computer Science Placement Test. Depending on appropriate Advanced Placement credit and/or results of the Computer Science Placement Test, entering students may place directly into 15-112 or 15-121 . 15-110 is taken as the first Computer Science prerequisite unless a student places directly into 15-112 or 15-121 . Students that do not gain a placement into 15-112 or 15-121 must begin the sequence with 15-110 and must complete it with a grade of D or above prior to entering 15-112 .

requirement_groups.name: Professional Communications
requirement_groups.source_instruction: Information systems professionals communicate with a wide range of people in most organizations and often facilitate communications between diverse groups of stakeholders. Consequently, the most successful professionals typically are those with strong communication skills. These courses help students see that the structure and presentation of information affects how well (and how easily) it can be understood and used. Complete one (1) of the following courses:

requirement_groups.name: Quantitative Analysis and Research Methods
requirement_groups.source_instruction: This area focuses on decision making and data analysis — essential to development of useful information systems.
